what_happened: The job to merge duplicate failure classes (instead of only adding new ones) was rejected at the final verdict. One of 6 acceptance criteria was unmet: the criterion that workspace-wide `cargo test`, clippy and fmt all pass. There were two major findings and no blockers. First, the evidence for behavior criterion 4 cites no commands that ran (D43). Second, workspace `cargo test` is red. The verifier says the cause predates this change and lies outside its scope: the xtask spec test (xtask/tests/spec.rs) fails because BRIEF.md and docs/spec.toml are out of step. One check failed: the test check, shard 4 of 6, xtask `--test spec`, with 6 of 30 tests failing. All six are brief-coverage tests (for example the_real_spec_covers_every_heading_and_addendum_of_the_brief). The failed check and the unmet criterion are different things. The criterion was unmet because that check was red.
cause: A repo-wide test criterion was put on a job whose scope has nothing to do with the failing area, and nothing recorded a baseline of main's test state before the job began. BRIEF.md and docs/spec.toml had drifted apart earlier, probably through a hand edit of a governing file, so the spec coverage tests were already red. The job could not fix that within its scope, yet a green workspace was a condition of acceptance, so correct work was rejected with no way to tell whether the job caused the failure. The producer is also not required to cite the commands it ran as evidence, so the D43 finding came on top of it.
prevention: Before dispatching a job, run the workspace checks on the base commit and record which tests already fail. Judge the "tests pass" criterion against that baseline: a failure present on the base counts as pre-existing and does not make the criterion unmet. Athena should raise it as a separate repair item for the BRIEF.md and docs/spec.toml mismatch. It should also block further jobs until that is fixed, or require the producer to list the commands it ran so the D43 evidence rule is met.
proposed_request: Merge duplicate failure classes in the introspection registry instead of only adding new ones, so that when a new case fits an existing class it is filed there. First, on a clean checkout of main, run `cargo test` and note which tests already fail. The xtask spec tests (xtask/tests/spec.rs: the_real_spec_covers_every_heading_and_addendum_of_the_brief and five related coverage tests) currently fail because BRIEF.md and docs/spec.toml are out of step. If they still fail, add the missing requirements to docs/spec.toml for the BRIEF.md headings that are uncovered, as a separate first change in this job, so that workspace `cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check` all pass. Acceptance: (1) duplicate classes in the registry are merged under one id, and earlier cases that point at a merged-away id are re-pointed to the surviving one; (2) the introspection prompt tells the writer to prefer an existing class over a new one; (3) the spec coverage tests pass, and the evidence for each behavior criterion cites the exact commands that ran and their results.
